ms.report:
(A) We created a CI/CD pipeline for our wallet. This allows us to automatically build and test the wallet for each new release. While the setup of a CI/CD pipeline is by itself not usual or special, it is a required step which took some work. Ed is demonstrating and explaining the pipeline in a video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qQhB-29cSRw&ab_channel=LivelyGig

(B) We made a major change in the wallets architecture to support multiple DIDs. The previous architecture was focused solely on supporting just a single DID (which was good enough a proof-of-concept). Ed demonstrates the new feature in this video and also explains why it was such an important work item: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rhN2ug0AMWU&ab_channel=LivelyGig

(C) We created a GitHub Repo for everyone to download and test the newest release of the wallet. You’ll find it here, with instructions on how to install the wallet: https://github.com/bsandmann/blocktrust-identity-wallet

(D) With the requirement of having multiple DIDs, we also had to change the UI and the workflow of the wallet. As this is not just a change in the ‘backend’ of the wallet but obvious to the user, we do not provide any additional evidence that changes were made. If in doubt, please compare an earlier walkthrough of the wallet with the video provided in (B).

(E) This section consists of two parts. First, we created a backup & restore feature in the wallet. This allows the user to back up the complete wallet contents (Seed phrase, DIDs, Verifiable Credentials) into an encrypted data object. When opening a new wallet (e.g. on a another device) the user can then use the newly created “restore” feature to import the encrypted wallet. After importing, the user is redirected to unlock the encrypted wallet with his password. A simple description of the feature with screenshots can be found here: https://blocktrust.dev/downloads/Progressreport_Identity_Wallet_February_2023.pdf

ms.promise:
(A) We would like to provide a way for users, to use the wallet, to log-in into a website using a DID. To accomplish that, we’ll provide JS code snippets which can be integrated into a website by the developers. 
(B) Signing-in is a very specific process. We would also provide a more general functionality to sign a request from a website with the private key of a DID. 
(C) Also, we would like to add functionality inside the wallet to share credentials with a website. 
(D) The interaction between identity-wallets and websites has to be standardized at some point. Also, the import and export functionality has to be identical between different Cardano-SSI-Wallets. We’ll engage with other wallets-teams to find common ground. 
(E) Before finishing the project, we plan to conduct a security/code review.
ms.criteria:
(A) A small JavaScript snippet is available for developers to integrate into their website to allow the features of (B) and (C). 
(B) The communication between a website with the SDK and the wallet works reliable without any hacks and workarounds. 
(C) Same as (B). 
(D) We hope to find a common standard between the different teams. This may happen only partially at first. 
(E) The security/code review finds no major issues. If so, the issues will be resolved.
ms.report:
---------
 PoA was intially submitted in the middle of June 2023. Due to remarks in the the review from IOG we submitted a change request which was accepted. This PoA is the same as in June but should now pass due to the small changes.
---------
(A) Initially, we aimed to offer developers an SDK for integrating our wallet into their websites, essentially serving as a dApp-Connector for the identity wallet. However, following thorough research and evaluation of various solutions, we decided to utilize PRISM's upcoming enterprise feature, 'PRISM onboard and authenticate'. This service, designed to replace the need for an SDK, offers HTTP endpoints instead. Despite some limitations, we adopted this approach to prevent ecosystem fragmentation and to find a common solution.
Now, instead of an SDK, developers need to integrate various JavaScript snippets. While not overly complex, this task is not trivial either. Therefore, we've created documentation that includes a general overview of website interaction (https://identitywallet.blocktrust.dev/websiteInteraction/Overview), a walkthrough for non-developers (https://identitywallet.blocktrust.dev/websiteInteraction/AtalaPrismSignIn), and detailed technical documentation for developers (https://identitywallet.blocktrust.dev/developers/AtalaPrism), which includes the necessary JavaScript snippets.

(B) + (C) We've produced a video demonstrating our wallet's sign-in process and the website prepared to support the PRISM onboard and authenticate service. You can view the video here: https://youtu.be/X1yAkg4Qygc.

(D) Over recent months, we've been in dialogue with several parties attempting to develop their own sign-in solutions. It became apparent that aside from our and PRISM's solutions, there are few functional DID-based solutions not just theoretical or crypto-based. ms.promise: A working browser-extension-wallet for Atala PRISM. It can be downloaded in a web store and installed by any user. The wallet allows the user to create a single (or multiple) DIDs and receive credentials (VCs). It offers the functionality to back up and restore credentials, as well as log-in with a DID. We also will be building a website explaining the wallet and provide a JS SDK with documentation for developers to integrate it into their website to offer the log-in functionality to their users. These are just the minimum features we are committed to regarding the final milestone. Additional features will be added along the way. To finish the project, we'll provide the link to the wallet-website, the link to the developer documentation and the JS-SDK. Also we'll provide links to the different webstores which listed the wallet.A at least 5-min long videos, showing all the major features of the wallet.
ms.criteria:
(A) The wallet will be submitted to the web stores of the major browser-vendors for review. We do believe that we are able to deliver a good and stable product in this timeframe. But a wallet is a complicated and ever-changing product. Also, the release is pretty new and likely won’t be able to collect extensive feedback from the first users in this timeframe. For this reason, we might be labeling the wallet as a “developer-release” for the first months. 
(B) A website for the wallet is created (documentation, explanation). This page serves as an introduction to the blocktrust identity wallet
